data.name: Melchiora
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Melchiora means 'queen of the south', and in Greek, it means 'reigning one'. In the Bible, Melchiora is mentioned in the Old Testament as the queen of Sheba who traveled from Ethiopia to visit King Solomon. Her name symbolizes the wisdom and wealth she brought with her.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes wisdom and wealth brought to us by God.

in_hebrew.name: מְלֶכִיאֹר
in_hebrew.meaning: מלכי כוח, שם של רצון, כוח וגבורה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מקור השם ביהדות, במקרא, ובברית החדשה. 'מְלֶכִיאֹר' היא צורה נשית של שם הגבר 'מְלֶכִי' שפירושו 'מלך' או 'כוח'. השם מופיע בספר דניאל במקרא כציון דמותה של אחת משלושת המלכים הקדושים. בברית החדשה, 'מְלֶכִיאֹר' הוא שם של אחד משלושת המלכים הקדושים, שהגיעו לבקר המלך הורדוס. הם הביאו חדשות על ילד תמידי שהוגדר כ'אדוננו ישוע'. השם 'מְלֶכִיאֹר' מיוחס גם לחסידות, ומשמעותו 'מלכות' או 'כוח'.

in_greek.name: Μελχιόρα
in_greek.meaning: μέλος της βασιλείας, δύναμις και τόκος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο ονομασία Μελχιόρα προέρχεται από το Εβραϊκό Μελχιορ. Είναι το γυναικείο όνομα της Μελχιώρ, που σημαίνει «μέλος της βασιλείας», «δύναμις» και «τόκος». Ο Μελχιώρ είναι ένα από τα τρία ονόματα των τριών Μελών της Κήρυκας, που έφτασαν από την Ανατολή για να ψάξουν τον Χριστό. Ο Μελχιώρ αντιπροσωπεύει την «Ευλογία» και την «Δύναμη». Η προέλευση του ονόματος Μελχιώρ εντοπίζεται στο Εβραϊκό «Μελχιορ», που σημαίνει «Μέλος της βασιλείας». Ο Μελχιώρ είναι επίσης συνδεδεμένος με την «Ευλογία» και την «Δύναμη».

in_latin.name: Melchiora
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Melchiora a Melchiore, nomine masculino, derivatur. Significat 'regni membrum', 'potestas' et 'generatio'. In Evangelio secundum Matthaeum, Melchiore, uno ex tribus Magis, nuntiavit adventum Domini. Per Melchiorem designatur potestas et virtus. Nomen Melchiora in historia Ecclesiae Christianae significat fidem et potestatem. In cultura Christiana, Melchiora repraesentat virtutem et fidem.

in_english.name: Melchiora
in_english.meaning: member of the kingdom, power and generation, one of the three wise men who brought gifts to the newborn Jesus
in_english.long_meaning: The name Melchiora is derived from the Hebrew name Melchi, meaning 'king' or 'power'. In the New Testament, Melchior is one of the three wise men who visited the newborn Jesus, bringing gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh. The name Melchiora is associated with power, authority, and spiritual significance. In Christian tradition, Melchiora represents faith, power, and spiritual growth. The name Melchiora is also linked to the qualities of strength, courage, and wisdom. It is a popular name among Christians, symbolizing the power of faith and the importance of following one's spiritual path.

data.cultural_impact: Melchiora's name has played an essential role in the history of Western civilization as it is a reminder of the ancient connections between Ethiopia and Israel. It highlights the importance of knowledge, exploration, and the exchange of ideas and goods between different cultures. The name evokes images of exotic lands, rich jewels, and profound wisdom, making it a popular choice for girls in many cultures.
data.spiritual_significance: Melchiora's name has a distinct spiritual meaning as it represents the journey of a wise and wealthy queen who sought out knowledge and, in turn, enriched her own life and the world around her. Melchiora could serve as a reminder for individuals to seek out wisdom and spiritual growth in their own lives, just as the queen did, and to strive for the creation of a more just and enlightened world. Additionally, the name could emphasize the importance of generosity, as the queen brought with her gifts of gold, incense, and myrrh. These virtues are still relevant and essential today, and they can inspire individuals to live their lives with compassion, generosity, and an open mind.

historical_references.reference: According to medieval European legend, the Magi, also referred to as the Three Wise Men or the Three Magi, were distinguished scholars from the East who followed a new star and came to pay homage to the infant Jesus. Melchior was one of them, traditionally considered to be the older and the king of the Magi. He was described as a descendant of the Babylonian priesthood and was believed to have been born in Persia.

Melchior is also mentioned in the 12th-century Latin grammatical work 'Doctrinalia' by John of Salisbury. In this text, Melchior is described as a magus who was a skilled mathematician and astrologer. The text includes a dialogue between Melchior and a certain Alcuin in which they discuss various mathematical and astronomical concepts.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Christian name 'Melchiora' has seen modern usage in various forms, primarily driven by the trends of feminization of names and name fusion. These trends are prevalent across multiple platforms, including social media handles, business names, and personal branding. For instance, a woman might use the name 'Melchiora' as a social media handle, or a business might be named 'Melchiora's Floral Boutique'. Name fusion, where two or more names are combined, can also occur, such as 'Melchiora Marie' or 'Melchiora Delacroix'.
